title: Work: What Do You Do?
overview:
Say what your job is.
Ask another person what they do.
Say when you start and finish.
Say if the work is hard or easy.
functions: Ask a person what they do
Say when you start and finish work
Say if work is hard or easy
Say when your day off is
learningPath: Patterns: I am a, and what do you do?
Say what you do. Record it.
Write four lines about your work.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 14. What do you do?
That question means: what is your job?
First, some jobs. Listen.
A teacher. A driver. A nurse.
A cleaner. A cook. A student.
Say them with me.
Now the pattern. Listen well.
I am a teacher.
Not: I am teacher. You need the word a.
I am a driver. I am a nurse.
Say it with me. I am a.
Now the question.
What do you do?
It sounds strange. It means: what is your job?
Say it with me. What do you do?
And the answer: I am a cook.
Now, where and when.
I work at a school.
I start at eight. I finish at four.
Say them with me. I start at. I finish at.
And the day you do not work: my day off.
My day off is Sunday.
Last, two describing words.
The work is hard. The work is easy.
And: I am busy today.
That is Unit 14. Go and say what you do.

grammar.title: I am a teacher
grammar.explanation:
English puts a small word before a job.
Most languages do not.
This is the mistake of the unit.
grammar.rule:
I am a teacher.
I am a driver.
I am a nurse.
I am a student.

She is a cook.
He is a cleaner.

am / is  +  a  +  job
grammar.workedExample:
Your job is driving a bus.
1. Start: I am.
2. Then the small word: a.
3. Then the job: driver.
4. Say: I am a driver.
5. Add more: I am a bus driver.
grammar.mistake:
No: I am teacher.
Yes: I am a teacher.
The word a is not optional here.
grammar.tip: Never leave out the a before a job.
grammar.practice:
Finish each one.
1. I am ___ nurse.
2. She is ___ cook.
3. He is ___ student.
4. I am ___ cleaner.
5. My father is ___ driver.
grammar.answers:
1. a
2. a
3. a
4. a
5. a
All five are a. That is the point of the card.

grammar.title: What do you do?
grammar.explanation:
A strange question with a simple meaning.
It does not mean what are you doing now.
It means: what is your job?
grammar.rule:
What do you do?
I am a nurse.

What does she do?
She is a teacher.

you, I, we, they → do
he, she, it → does
grammar.workedExample:
Someone asks what you do.
1. They want your job.
2. Answer with I am a.
3. Say: I am a cook.
4. Then ask back: And you? What do you do?
5. That keeps the conversation going.
grammar.mistake:
Do not answer with what you are doing now.
No: I am sitting.
Yes: I am a cook.
grammar.tip: Do for you. Does for he and she.
grammar.practice:
Write do or does.
1. What ___ you do?
2. What ___ she do?
3. What ___ they do?
4. What ___ he do?
5. ___ you work here?
grammar.answers:
1. do
2. does
3. do
4. does
5. Do
All five? He and she take does.

grammar.title: I start at eight
grammar.explanation:
Two verbs and a time.
The word at goes before a clock time.
grammar.rule:
I start work at eight.
I finish at four.

at eight
at nine
at half past five

Question: When do you start?
          What time do you finish?
grammar.workedExample:
You begin work at nine in the morning.
1. Start with I start work.
2. Then at.
3. Then the time: nine.
4. Say: I start work at nine.
5. Same for the end: I finish at five.
grammar.mistake:
No: I start work eight.
English needs at before a clock time.
Yes: I start work at eight.
grammar.tip: At goes before a clock time.
grammar.practice:
Finish each one.
1. I start ___ eight.
2. I finish ___ four.
3. The shop opens ___ nine.
4. The class starts ___ ten.
grammar.answers:
1. at
2. at
3. at
4. at
All four are at. Clock times always take at.

grammar.title: Hard, easy, busy
grammar.explanation:
Three words for how work feels.
They come after is or am.
grammar.rule:
The work is hard.
The work is easy.
I am busy.

It is a hard job.
It is an easy job.
It is a busy day.

Note: an easy job, because easy starts with a vowel sound.
grammar.workedExample:
Your day has a lot in it.
1. That is busy.
2. It is about you, so use am.
3. Say: I am busy today.
4. About the work, use is: The work is hard.
5. Both are right for the same day.
grammar.mistake:
Busy is about a person or a place.
Hard and easy are about the work.
No: I am hard. That means something else.
grammar.tip: I am busy. The work is hard.
grammar.practice:
Write am or is.
1. I ___ busy.
2. The work ___ hard.
3. The shop ___ busy.
4. It ___ an easy job.
5. I ___ not busy today.
grammar.answers:
1. am
2. is
3. is
4. is
5. am
Four or five right? Good.

readings.title: My Work

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — I am a
speaking.instructions:
Say each line out loud. Do not leave out the a.
1. I am a teacher.
2. I am a driver.
3. I am a nurse.
4. I am a student.
5. She is a cook.
6. He is a cleaner.
Now say your own: I am a ___.
Tap the mic. Say all seven.
Check: the word a in every one?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor what your job is. Ask what a nurse does.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say each line out loud. Do not leave out the a.
One. I am a teacher.
Two. I am a driver.
Three. I am a nurse.
Four. I am a student.
Five. She is a cook.
Six. He is a cleaner.
Now say your own. I am a ...
Tap the mic. Say all seven.
Check: the word a in every one?

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — What do you do?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: What do you do? B: I am a nurse. And you?
2. A: I am a driver. B: Where do you work?
3. A: At the hospital. B: When do you start?
4. A: At seven. B: That is early. Is it hard?
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you ask back in line 1?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor what it does. Answer when it asks you.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — When I start and finish
speaking.instructions:
Say four lines about your day.
1. I start at ___.
2. I finish at ___.
3. My day off is ___.
4. The work is ___.
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: at before every clock time?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor when you start and finish. Ask about its hours.
speaking.instructionsSpeech:
Say four lines about your day.
One. I start at ...
Two. I finish at ...
Three. My day off is ...
Four. The work is ...
Tap the mic. Say the four lines.
Check: at before every clock time?

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Hard or easy?
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Say hard or easy for you.
1. Learning English.
2. Getting up at six.
3. Counting to twenty.
4. Saying the alphabet.
5. Understanding fast English.
6. Writing your name.
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Say a whole line: It is hard. Or: It is easy.
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor two things that are hard and two that are easy.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Telling the boss
speaking.instructions:
You are ill. Read A. Say B.
1. A: Hello? B: Good morning. This is (your name).
2. A: Yes? B: I am ill. I cannot come today.
3. A: I am sorry. B: I will come tomorrow.
4. A: All right. B: Thank you. Goodbye.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you say your name first?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor you are ill and cannot work. Listen to the answer.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The er ending
speaking.instructions:
Many jobs end the same way. Listen.
teach-ER ... driv-ER ... clean-ER ... work-ER
The ending is quiet and short. Not ER. Just uh.
The first part is strong.
Now say: I am a teacher. I am a cleaner.
Tap the mic. Say both lines.
Check: is the ending quiet?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor for three jobs that end in er.

writing.title: Writing 1 — My work
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about your work or your study.
Say what you do, where, and when.
writing.model:
I am a cleaner.
I work at a school.
I start at six.
My day off is Sunday.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
The word a before the job.
At before every clock time.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line saying if the work is hard or easy.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A note for the boss
writing.prompt:
You are ill. Write three short lines for your boss.
Say who you are. Say you are ill. Say when you come.
writing.model:
This is Ana.
I am ill today.
I will come tomorrow.
writing.criteria:
Three lines.
Your name is in the first one.
You say you are ill.
You say when you will come.
writing.support: Write two lines: your name, and that you are ill.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Put in the a
activities.instructions:
Write a or an.
1. I am ___ nurse.
2. She is ___ cook.
3. He is ___ student.
4. I am ___ cleaner.
5. My father is ___ driver.
6. It is ___ easy job.
activities.answers:
1. a
2. a
3. a
4. a
5. a
6. an
Five or six right: good. Easy starts with a vowel sound, so an.

activities.title: Practice 3 — When do you start?
activities.instructions:
Write at where it is needed.
1. I start ___ eight.
2. I finish ___ four.
3. The shop opens ___ nine.
4. The class starts ___ ten.
5. I finish late ___ Friday.
6. My day off is ___ Sunday.
activities.answers:

2. at
3. at
4. at
5. on (a day takes on)
6. on
Four or more right: good.
Clock times take at. Days take on.

activities.instructions:
Write do or does.

2. What ___ she do?
3. What ___ they do?
4. What ___ he do?
5. ___ you work here?
6. ___ he work at night?
activities.answers:
1. do
2. does
3. do
4. does
5. Do
6. Does
Five or six right: good. He and she take does.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Am or is?
activities.instructions:
Write am or is.
1. I ___ busy.
2. The work ___ hard.
3. The shop ___ busy.
4. It ___ an easy job.
5. I ___ not busy today.
6. My boss ___ kind.
activities.answers:
1. am
2. is
3. is
4. is
5. am
6. is
Five or six right: good.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read the notice
activities.instructions:
Read Hours and Days Off again.
1. What time do you start?
2. What time do you finish?
3. Which days are off?
4. You are ill. Who do you tell?
5. By what time?
activities.answers:
1. Eight
2. Four
3. Saturday and Sunday
4. The boss
5. Before eight
Four or five right: you can read a workplace notice.
activities.solo: Read it, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: A person who helps ill people is a ___.
quizzes.why: A nurse helps ill people. A cook makes food.

quizzes.q: A person who is learning is a ___.
quizzes.why: A student learns. A teacher helps them learn.
English needs a before a job.
Cook starts with a consonant sound, so a.
Easy starts with a vowel sound, so an.

quizzes.q: What does the question What do you do? ask?
quizzes.why: It asks about your work, not about this moment.
A clock time takes at. A day takes on.
A day of the week takes on.

quizzes.q: You have a lot to do today. You are ___.
quizzes.why: Busy is about a person. Hard is about the work.

quizzes.q: The work takes a lot from you. It is ___.
quizzes.why: Hard describes the work, not the person.

quizzes.q: The day you do not work is your ___.
quizzes.why: A day off is a day with no work.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: The missing a is the mistake of this unit
teacherNotes.note: I am teacher is understood and it is also the single clearest marker of a beginner. Most languages do not put an article before a job. Pattern 1 exists only for that one word and it is worth the whole card.

teacherNotes.type: What do you do? is idiomatic, not literal
teacherNotes.note: Learners reasonably answer I am sitting. Say plainly that the question is a fixed phrase meaning what is your job, and teach the answer beside it.

teacherNotes.type: Work is not a safe topic for everyone
teacherNotes.note: Some adult learners are not working, are working below their qualifications, or cannot say what they do. Let I am a student or I am looking for work stand as full answers, and teach them as such rather than as a fallback.

teacherNotes.type: Speaking 5 is the one they will use first
teacherNotes.note: Phoning a boss to say you are ill is a real task with real consequences, and it needs only four short lines. Practise it more than the job words.

assignment.title: What I do
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Say four lines about your work or study.
Say what you do, where, and when you start.
Then ask: And you? What do you do?
2. Write three lines for a boss, saying you are ill.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
